Maya (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need to add SM occupancy and GPU queue-depth to the telemetry feed for both Hosted + Dedicated pools. Can we align on schema and rollout?
Jin (eng-infra): +1. What's the target cardinality? per-instance labels blow up cost.
Arjun (eng-runtime): We can emit at three granularities: pool-level, model-level, and instance-level. Default ingest should be pool+model; instance-level only for debug windows.
Priya (eng-ml): For model perf analysis we need model and seq_len buckets. SM occupancy correlates strongly with tail latency for long sequences.
Maya (eng-platform): Agreed. Proposal: expose `gpu_sm_occupancy` (0..1), `gpu_mem_used_bytes`, and `gpu_queue_depth` with labels: pool, pool_type (hosted|dedicated), model, region, and optional tenant when Dedicated.
Sam (product): Why optional tenant? We need per-customer cost/usage on Dedicated for billing signals.
Jin (eng-infra): For Hosted we intentionally avoid per-tenant instance labels for privacy and cost. For Dedicated we can include `tenant_id` but sampled/with PII controls. Also add `pool_id` for routing maps.
Bea (devex): For console dashboards we want: 1) pool-level time series, 2) model-level breakdown, 3) top N tenants by queue depth (Dedicated). Also an alert when avg occupancy > 0.9 for 5m.
Arjun (eng-runtime): Now the internal API: current telemetry agent pushes metrics via our metrics-gateway `/v1/metrics/ingest`. We should extend payload to accept `metric_name`, `value`, and `labels` JSON map. Debate: keep Prometheus-like flat labels or nested dimensions? I vote flat labels to keep compatibility.
Priya (eng-ml): Flat labels are easier for Prometheus-compatible backends. Example payload:
```
metric: gpu_sm_occupancy
value: 0.72
labels: {pool: "hosted", pool_id: "h-1", model: "redwood/open-6b", region: "us-west-2"}
```
Jin (eng-infra): We should also decide scrape/push frequency. Runtime can emit per-instance every 15s, but we should aggregate to 60s before store to reduce cardinality/cost.
Maya (eng-platform): Sounds right. Emit high-res internally (15s) but aggregator downsampler to 60s for ingestion. Also add a sampled 1s window for debugging when tenant flags `debug_metrics=true`.
Sam (product): Can we add a derived metric `effective_utilization` that accounts for batching (i.e., SM busy time excluding KV cache stalls)? Product wants to correlate with cost per token.
Arjun (eng-runtime): We can expose `gpu_sm_busy_fraction` and `gpu_sm_stall_fraction`. Derived `effective_utilization = busy_fraction - stall_fraction` can be computed at query time in dashboards.
Bea (devex): Dashboard UX: add a compare toggle Hosted vs Dedicated, and a heatmap for queue depth by pool. Also a per-route view (map route->model->pool) so customers can see which routes hit high queue depth.
Priya (eng-ml): Important: when rolling out across Dedicated we must version metric labels. If we change `gpu_sm_occupancy` -> `gpu_sm_utilization` later, we need to emit both for a period. Add `metric_version` label maybe.
Maya (eng-platform): Good call. Let's add `metric_version` label default `v1`. We can deprecate later with a planned 30-day overlap.
Jin (eng-infra): Ops constraints: aggregator must enforce a max of 25 custom label combinations per minute per pool to avoid card explosion from noisy tenants. We will also cap ingestion rate per project.
Arjun (eng-runtime): For queue depth we need to define semantics: number of pending inference requests per GPU device, or per worker queue? I'd prefer per-worker queue (worker maps 1:1 to device in Dedicated, but not always in Hosted).
Priya (eng-ml): We need both: `gpu_queue_depth_device` and `gpu_queue_depth_worker`. Keep worker-level as primary, device-level for Dedicated where device assignment is fixed.
Maya (eng-platform): Example Prom labels we discussed in docs for the console team:
```
gpu_sm_occupancy{pool="hosted",pool_id="h-1",model="redwood/open-6b",region="us-west-2"} 0.72
gpu_queue_depth_worker{pool="dedicated",pool_id="d-42",tenant_id="acme",worker_id="w-7"} 5
```
Bea (devex): Who's owning the dashboard templates? I'll build initial panels if eng-platform provides the queries and aggregated endpoints.
Maya (eng-platform): I'll own the metric contract doc and the aggregator changes. Jin will own ingestion-side rate-limiting and storage concerns. Bea will make the panels. Priya will validate ML correlation signals. Arjun will change runtime to emit new metrics.
Jin (eng-infra): Timeline? Can we get an initial alpha landed in Hosted next week (only pool-level + model-level)? Then Dedicated rollout over 2 sprints with tenant labeling gated by compliance review.
Arjun (eng-runtime): Alpha for Hosted pool+model metrics: runtime patch ready in 2 days. Need CI for aggregator tests.
Priya (eng-ml): I'll prepare a small evaluation set to validate occupancy vs tail-latency for open-6b and long-seq workloads.
Sam (product): Make sure Console has an opt-in beta flag for customers to view new panels — we don't want to expose debug details by default.
Maya (eng-platform): Action items:
- Maya: write metric contract doc (link to be posted) and add `metric_version` rule.
- Arjun: runtime PR to emit metrics (15s internal, aggregator-friendly labels).
- Jin: aggregation/downsampling service changes + doc on cardinality limits.
- Bea: dashboard templates + alert rules (occupancy > 0.9 5m, queue_depth > threshold per pool).
- Priya: evaluation harness and regression checks.
telemetry-bot: deploy status: telemetry-aggregator-v2 deployed to staging at 1791234700 :white_check_mark:
Bea (devex): I'll wait for staging metrics to appear and then start wiring panels. Ping me when staging has `gpu_sm_occupancy` + `gpu_queue_depth_worker`.
Maya (eng-platform): I'll post the contract doc here in an hour. If no objections to labels/versions we'll proceed.
Jin (eng-infra): One last note: we should tag Dedicated tenant_id values as PII and ensure KMS-encrypted storage. I'll add to infra checklist.
Priya (eng-ml): Thanks all. This will help a lot for capacity planning and routing policy tweaks.
Sam (product): :thumbsup: excited to see per-route heatmaps.
Arjun (eng-runtime): I'll open the runtime PR now and @Maya for review.
Maya (eng-platform): Thanks — closing the loop once doc is up.
